text:
MacKenzie Weegar is doing almost everything right in Utah except getting rewarded for it. The Mammoth have controlled 59% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) with him on the ice at five on five, and he's eating 22 minutes a night, with 58 blocked shots and 65 hits through 22 games.

The goals haven't followed. Utah has scored 13.0 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Weegar on the ice, and it has cost him: 1 point in his last ten on 3.5 expected, during a stretch when the team won twice. That kind of gap usually swings back, and our numbers flag him as due.

Last season told a similar story. Evolving-Hockey had him at -1.8 wins above replacement, but -0.7 on expected goals: the chances were there, the finishing wasn't. The one real ding was penalties, which cost him 2.1 goals. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him moving the puck out cleanly, 49% of exits with possession.

A seventh-round pick from 2013 with 629 games behind him, he's a steadier player than his 5 points say.
